# Nivra 0.1.0-alpha.7

## AI-first Game Development

- Game Development is rebuilt around one practical loop: open a Unity project, connect Unity, give the agent a mission, and validate the result.
- New Unity cockpit with Scene preview, hierarchy, selected-object inspector, Console, Play/Pause/Stop, scene save, Asset refresh and GameObject creation.
- Nivra automatically installs the local Unity Bridge and starts the matching Unity Editor when available. No separate project initialization step.
- The agent receives the local game brief, current milestone, active scene, selected GameObject, Console errors and live Unity status.
- New local game brief for concept, genre, target platform, perspective, visual direction, milestone and constraints. It is stored outside the repository.
- Unity controls are disabled with a clear reason until the required connection is ready; dead or misleading actions have been removed.
- Scene View captures can update automatically and be attached to the AI chat for visual validation.
- Project health, GitHub and tool setup are available in secondary tabs without cluttering the main workflow.

## Project and Windows reliability

- Open Project is sufficient; Nivra discovers skills, rules and project state automatically.
- Multiple projects can be opened in separate Nivra windows.
- Background Git, PowerShell, CMD, Codex and Claude processes remain hidden.
- Unity polling uses a lightweight live endpoint instead of repeatedly scanning Git and the full toolchain.

## Release reliability

- The alpha.7 publisher safely backs up local release-repository changes, restores the public repository to origin/main and then publishes.
- Private signing keys and other ignored release-server files are not removed.
